paper.title: RIPEMD-160: a strengthened version of RIPEMD

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or standard; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: RIPEMD-160 of the 9 messages in the paper's Appendix B ("", "a", "abc", "message digest", the lowercase alphabet, the 56-character message, upper+lower+digits, 8 times "1234567890", and 1 million times "a") gives the 9 published 160-bit digests

expected_values_source.what: the 9 RIPEMD-160 test values of Appendix B of the paper, and the selection, rotation and constant tables of its Appendix A pseudo-code (extracted from the PDF text as numbers; the constants K' and K were also checked on the host to equal the paper's floor(2^30 * sqrt or cube root) definitions)
expected_values_source.note: digests and tables are data, copied as numbers; no third-party code was copied

negative_control: built with -DRMD_S0=12 (first left-line rotation amount changed from 11 to 12), 0 of 9 values match and the program exits 1
not_checked: security claims (the paper's design rationale and analysis of collision resistance)
RIPEMD-128 (the paper lists test values for it but gives no pseudo-code in the appendix; not implemented)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
messages beyond the 9 in Appendix B
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 9 RIPEMD-160 digests published in the paper's Appendix B. It does not show the security claims hold.
